cards: King Wu of Zhou defeats Di Xin at the Battle of Muye
The First Emperor of Qin standardises the Chinese script across his empire
Xu Shen completes the Shuowen Jiezi, the first dictionary to analyse the structure of characters
The Diamond Sutra in Chinese, the earliest dated printed book, is made in China
King Sejong of Korea promulgates the Hangul alphabet as an alternative to Chinese characters
The Kangxi Dictionary is completed, listing more than 47,000 characters
China’s Ministry of Education orders primary schools to teach the vernacular instead of Classical Chinese
Duke Huan takes the throne and appoints Guan Zhong as minister
Duke Huan presides over the covenant of Kuiqiu as hegemon
The Zhou king recognises Tian He as ruler of Qi
Sun Bin's strategy defeats Wei at the Battle of Maling
Yue Yi's coalition army sacks Linzi
Tian Dan breaks the siege of Jimo and restores Qi
King Jian surrenders to Qin, completing the Qin unification
King Wu defeats the Shang at the Battle of Muye
King Li is driven out and the Gonghe regency begins
King Xuan begins a revival against the Xianyun and the Huaiyi
The Quanrong and the Marquis of Shen sack Haojing and kill King You
Xiong Tong proclaims himself king as King Wu of Chu
King Zhuang defeats Jin at the Battle of Bi
The State of Wu defeats Chu at Boju and occupies Ying
Nobles kill the reformer Wu Qi after the death of King Dao
Bai Qi of Qin captures Ying; the capital moves to Chen
Chu moves its capital to Shouchun

Shang Yang begins his reforms under Duke Xiao
Qin conquers Ba and Shu in the Sichuan basin

Zheng takes the title of First Emperor

Saka troops fight in the Persian centre at the Battle of Marathon
Alexander the Great defeats a Saka force at the Jaxartes

Emperor Wu of Han establishes official chairs for the Five Classics

Zhang Daoling receives a revelation from the deified Laozi and founds the Way of the Celestial Masters

The Quanzhen master Qiu Chuji meets Genghis Khan in the Hindu Kush
The Ming court completes the printing of the Daoist Canon
Modu seizes power from his father Touman and unites the Xiongnu

The Han accept the heqin treaty of gifts and royal brides in exchange for peace
A failed Han ambush at Mayi ends the policy of appeasement
Wei Qing and Huo Qubing defeat the Xiongnu at the Battle of Mobei
Chanyu Huhanye travels to Chang'an and acknowledges Han overlordship
The confederation splits into Southern and Northern Xiongnu
The Northern Xiongnu suffer a crushing defeat by Han forces and their allies
The first ritual rebuilding of the Grand Shrine of Ise
The Kojiki records the myths of the kami and the descent of the emperors from the sun goddess
The Engishiki lists 2,861 shrines and the court’s rituals and prayers
The Meiji government orders the separation of kami and buddhas
The shrine later named Yasukuni is founded in Tokyo for those who died fighting for the emperor
The Allied occupation’s Shinto Directive ends State Shinto
Modu, once a hostage of the Yuezhi, seizes power among the Xiongnu
Modu Chanyu takes power and unites the Xiongnu, founding the first great empire of the eastern steppe

Amid a Xiongnu civil war, Huhanye pays homage in person at Chang’an and accepts Han overlordship
Bumin Qaghan overthrows the Rouran and founds the First Turkic Khaganate
A kurultai at the source of the Onon river proclaims Temüjin Genghis Khan of the Mongols

Qing armies crush the last Dzungar resistance, ending the last great nomadic empire of the steppe
Liu Bang defeats Xiang Yu and proclaims himself emperor as Gaozu
Emperor Wu takes the throne, beginning the dynasty's most expansive reign
The Imperial Academy is founded to train officials in the Confucian classics
Wei Qing and Huo Qubing drive Xiongnu power beyond the Gobi Desert
The Han census records a population of nearly 60 million
The dynasty is restored as the Eastern Han after Wang Mang's usurpation
The Yellow Turban Rebellion erupts amid famine and peasant displacement
Cao Pi deposes Emperor Xian and declares the Wei dynasty, ending the Han
Xianbei warriors kill the Northern Xiongnu chanyu Youliu
Tanshihuai routs a three-pronged Han expedition into the steppe
Kebineng marches to Beidi in support of Zhuge Liang

Traditional founding of Saro by Bak Hyeokgeose

King Jinheung seizes the Han River valley from Baekje
Silla conquers Daegaya, the last Gaya state

Silla and Tang take Pyongyang and destroy Goguryeo

Traditional founding of Goguryeo by Jumong at Jolbon

Buddhism is received and the Taehak academy founded under King Sosurim
King Jangsu erects the stele of Gwanggaeto the Great at Ji'an
The capital moves from Gungnae to Pyongyang
Jangsu takes the Baekje capital Hanseong
Eulji Mundeok routs a Sui army at the Salsu River
Tang and Silla forces take Pyongyang; the kingdom ends
Traditional founding of Baekje by Onjo at Wiryeseong
Geunchogo's army kills the Goguryeo king Gogugwon at Pyongyang
The monk Marananta brings Buddhism from the Eastern Jin
Goguryeo takes Hanseong; the court moves to Ungjin
King Seong moves the capital to Sabi
King Seong is killed fighting Silla at Gwansanseong
Silla and Tang take Sabi; King Uija surrenders
Tang and Silla defeat Baekje loyalists and a Yamato fleet at Baekgang
A Kushan army crossing the Pamirs is repulsed by the Han general Ban Chao
An embassy from the Kushan king, probably Vasudeva I, reaches the Wei court
Sima Rui takes the imperial title at Jiankang as Emperor Yuan
Huan Wen conquers the Cheng Han state in Sichuan
Wang Xizhi writes his preface at the Orchid Pavilion gathering
Jin forces defeat the Former Qin at the Battle of Fei River
Sun En's Daoist rebellion breaks out in the coastal south
Huan Xuan usurps the throne as emperor of Chu
Liu Yu's army conquers the Later Qin and takes Chang'an
Emperor Gong abdicates to Liu Yu, founder of the Liu Song
Shelun takes the title khagan after conquering the Gaoche
Rouran cavalry raid the Northern Wei centre of Shengle
Emperor Taiwu of Northern Wei routs the khagan Datan in Mongolia
The Rouran install Kan Bozhou as king of Gaochang
The Gaoche break away under Afuzhiluo
Anagui flees to the Northern Wei, which later restores him

Bilge Qaghan is poisoned by one of his own ministers
Uyghurs, Karluks and Basmyls seize Otuken and kill the last Gokturk qaghan

Li Shimin kills his brothers at the Xuanwu Gate and becomes Emperor Taizong
The Tang destroy the Eastern Turkic Khaganate; Taizong is hailed as Heavenly Khagan
Wu Zetian proclaims her own Zhou dynasty, interrupting Tang rule until 705
Abbasid forces defeat Gao Xianzhi's Tang army at the Battle of Talas
An Lushan rebels, capturing Luoyang and Chang'an and forcing Xuanzong to flee
Zhu Wen deposes the last Tang emperor and founds the Later Liang
Princess Wencheng of Tang China arrives as a bride for the Tibetan royal house
Tibet conquers the Tuyuhun around Lake Kokonor
Tibetans defeat a Tang army at the Dafei River and overrun the Tarim Basin
A Tibetan army occupies the Tang capital Chang'an for about two weeks
Emperor Udumtsen (Langdarma) is assassinated and the empire breaks apart
The Khazars destroy an Arab army at Marj Ardabil
Marwan ibn Muhammad's great campaign forces a temporary Khazar submission
Dae Joyeong defeats a Tang army at Tianmenling and founds the state of Jin

The first Balhae embassy reaches Japan
A Balhae fleet raids Dengzhou in Shandong
King Seon begins a reign of northern expansion
King Dae Inseon surrenders to the Khitan; Balhae becomes the client state of Dongdan
Bumin founds the Turkic Khaganate, the first state to bear the name Türk

Yusuf Khass Hajib completes the Kutadgu Bilig, the first great Islamic work in Turkic
Vilhelm Thomsen deciphers the Old Turkic runic script

Nasr ibn Ali takes Bukhara and ends the Samanid Empire
Mahmud of Ghazni defeats the Kara-Khanids near Balkh

Abaoji proclaims himself emperor of the Khitan

Yelü Deguang takes Kaifeng and adopts the dynastic name Liao
The Treaty of Chanyuan brings annual Song payments of silver and silk
The wooden Sakyamuni Pagoda at Yingxian is completed
Wanyan Aguda proclaims the Jin dynasty and routs the Liao at Hubudagang
The Jin capture the last Liao emperor, Tianzuo
Wang Geon is raised to the throne and founds Goryeo
Taejo defeats Later Baekje, completing the reunification of the peninsula
Gang Gam-chan destroys a Khitan army at the Battle of Gwiju
Military officers seize power and depose King Uijong
The court withdraws to Ganghwa Island during the Mongol invasions
Carving of the Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks is completed
Yi Seong-gye deposes King Gongyang and founds Joseon
Zhao Kuangyin seizes power in the Chenqiao Mutiny and founds the Song Dynasty

Wang Anshi launches the New Policies to reform state finances
The Jurchen Jin capture Kaifeng and carry off emperors Huizong and Qinzong
Southern Song fleets defeat the Jin at Tangdao and Caishi
The Mongols begin the five-year siege of Xiangyang
Lin'an surrenders and the boy emperor Gong is taken north
The loyalist fleet is destroyed at Yamen, ending the Song Dynasty
Sabuktigin is chosen as leader of the Turkic garrison at Ghazni
Mahmud takes Khurasan and is recognised by the Abbasid caliph
Mahmud defeats the Hindu Shahi king Jayapala near Peshawar
Mahmud sacks the temple of Somnath
The Seljuks defeat Mas'ud I at the Battle of Dandanaqan
The Ghurids take Lahore, ending the dynasty
Wanyan Aguda proclaims the Great Jin
Jin capture the Liao emperor Tianzuo, ending the Liao state
Jin take Kaifeng and carry off two Song emperors
The Treaty of Shaoxing fixes the Song border on the Huai River
Prince Hailing moves the capital to Zhongdu (Beijing)
Genghis Khan invades and defeats the Jin at Yehuling
Caizhou falls and Emperor Aizong takes his own life
Goryeo’s generals seize power in Korea and rule through their council while kings reign as figureheads
Soldiers expel England’s Rump Parliament; army officers draft a constitution making Oliver Cromwell Lord Protector
Spaniards form local and national juntas to resist Napoleon’s invasion, the councils from which the modern term derives

Ethiopia’s military council, the Derg, deposes Emperor Haile Selassie and rules until 1987
Argentina’s armed forces seize power; defeat in the Falklands War of 1982 forces them to hold elections in 1983
Myanmar’s armed forces seize power in a coup on 1 February, their third takeover since 1958
Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan at a kurultai on the Mongolian steppe
Subutai and Jebe defeat the Rus and Kipchaks at the Kalka River
Mongol armies defeat Polish and Hungarian forces at Legnica and Mohi
Hülegü sacks Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate
Kublai's death removes the last Great Khan widely recognised across the empire
The Ming drive the Yuan dynasty out of China
Chagatai Khan begins his rule over the appanage allotted by Genghis Khan
Alghu exploits the Mongol civil war to assert real independence
Qutlugh Khwaja leads a great Chagataid army to the outskirts of Delhi
Eastern nomadic tribes revolt against Tarmashirin and overthrow him
Timur completes his seizure of power in Transoxiana
The Yarkent Khanate is founded as a Chagataid successor state
Batu withdraws to the lower Volga and establishes his ulus
Uzbek Khan begins a reign in which Islam becomes the state religion
Plague strikes Janibeg's army besieging Caffa
Dmitry of Moscow defeats Mamai at the Battle of Kulikovo
Timur defeats Tokhtamysh on the Terek and sacks Sarai
The Great Stand on the Ugra River ends Moscow's tribute
Meñli I Giray of Crimea defeats the last khan and sacks Sarai
Kublai's claim to be Great Khan sparks civil war with his brother Ariq Böke
Kublai Khan adopts the dynastic name Da Yuan
Xiangyang falls to Mongol counterweight trebuchets after a five-year siege
The first Mongol invasion of Japan is wrecked by storms
The last Song loyalist fleet is destroyed at Yamen, leaving the Yuan masters of all China
The Yellow River bursts its dykes, devastating the North China Plain
The Red Turban Rebellion breaks out across the Huai and Yangtze valleys
Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming and Toghon Temür flees Dadu
Timur's army raises towers of skulls from the population of Isfahan
Timur defeats Tokhtamysh of the Golden Horde on the Terek
Timur sacks Delhi, leaving the city devastated for decades
Timur defeats and captures the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I at Ankara
Timur dies at Otrar while marching to invade Ming China
Ulugh Beg is put to death at the instigation of his own son
Abu Sa'id, last Timurid to reunite much of the realm, is killed fighting the Aq Qoyunlu
Muhammad Shaybani Khan takes Herat, ending Timurid rule
Zhu Yuanzhang defeats Chen Youliang at the naval battle of Lake Poyang
Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming dynasty and his armies take the Yuan capital, Dadu
Zheng He's first expedition sets out on voyages that reach East Africa by 1433
The Forbidden City is completed in the Yongle Emperor's new capital, Beijing
The Oirat Mongols capture the Zhengtong Emperor at Tumu
Li Zicheng takes Beijing; the Chongzhen Emperor takes his own life and the Qing occupy the city
The last Southern Ming loyalist regime comes to an end
Yi Seong-gye deposes the last Goryeo king and founds Joseon
King Sejong creates the Korean alphabet
The Gyeongguk daejeon law code is promulgated
Hideyoshi invades; Yi Sun-sin wins at Hansan Island
Injo surrenders to the Qing after the siege of Namhansanseong
The Treaty of Ganghwa opens Korea to Japan
Sho Hashi conquers Nanzan and completes the unification of Okinawa
The 'bridge of all nations' bell is cast for Shuri Castle
Kanemaru takes the throne as Sho En, founding the Second Sho dynasty
Sho Shin's forces defeat Oyake Akahachi and take control of the Yaeyama Islands
Satsuma invades and King Sho Nei surrenders Shuri
Tamagusuku Chokun's kumi odori dance-dramas are first performed for Chinese envoys
Commodore Perry signs a compact with the kingdom at Naha

Tauekel Khan takes Tashkent and Turkistan from Bukhara
Jahangir Khan checks the Dzungars at the Battle of Orbulaq
Dzungar invasion begins the 'Years of the Great Disaster'

Russia abolishes the khanship in the Middle Juz
Kenesary Kasymov, the last khan, is killed and his revolt ends

The siege of Osaka Castle destroys the Toyotomi house
Iemitsu formalises sankin-kotai, the alternate attendance of daimyo in Edo
Dutch traders are confined to the artificial island of Dejima in Nagasaki
Commodore Perry's 'Black Ships' enter Edo Bay demanding open ports
Shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu returns governing authority to Emperor Meiji
Imperial rule is restored and the Boshin War begins at Toba-Fushimi
Erdeni Batur joins the assembly that drafts the Mongol-Oirat Code
Galdan conquers the Yarkent Khanate and the Tarim Basin oases
Kangxi's armies defeat Galdan at the Battle of Jao Modo
Dzungar forces under Tsering Dondub sack Lhasa
Dzungar invasion of the Kazakh steppe begins the 'Great Disaster'

Qing armies reach the Ili valley; Amursana rebels
Nurhaci proclaims the Later Jin dynasty

Wu Sangui opens the Shanhai Pass and Qing forces capture Beijing

The Wuchang Uprising on 10 October begins the Xinhai Revolution

The Northern Expedition takes Beijing and the Nationalists reunify much of China
War with Japan begins after the Marco Polo Bridge Incident
Defeated in the civil war, the government moves to Taipei

First direct presidential election, won by Lee Teng-hui
Mao Zedong proclaims the People’s Republic in Beijing on 1 October
Chinese People’s Volunteers enter the Korean War
The Great Leap Forward begins, leading to the famine of 1959–61

The army crushes the Tiananmen Square protests on 4 June
